articles.title: How to Give Your AI Agent Memory You Can Audit
articles.excerpt: Giving an agent memory is easy. Knowing what it remembered, and whether that memory changed its answer, is the hard part. Most memory setups are a vector store behind a retrieval call. The agent recei…
articles.body: Giving an agent memory is easy. Knowing what it remembered, and whether that memory changed its answer, is the hard part. Most memory setups are a vector store behind a retrieval call. The agent receives some text, acts on it, and nobody records which memories were used. When the agent says something wrong, you cannot tell whether the model failed or a stale note from three months ago misled it. This guide shows how to build agent memory that stays inspectable, using ZizkaDB’s search and context functions. The principle is simple: memory should be part of the record, so every answer can be traced to the memories behind it.

articles.body: Many large employers — NVIDIA, Adobe, Salesforce and thousands more — run their careers sites on Workday. The addresses all look alike: https://<company>.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/<site> . If you follow hiring at a list of these companies, for a job board, a recruiting pipeline or your own job search, opening each site every day does not scale. This post shows how to turn any Workday careers site into clean JSON, and how to get only the jobs that are new since yesterday . 1. Find the careers site URL Open the company's careers page and click "Search for jobs". The address bar now shows the Workday site, for example: https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite That full URL is the safest input.

articles.title: Researchers have found a way to read the hidden thoughts of OpenAI's artificial intelligence
articles.excerpt: Security firm Xint demonstrated how OpenAI's conversation compaction feature could be used to extract a model's hidden reasoning into plain text. The technique bypassed cross-model replay blocks by ut…
articles.body: Security firm Xint demonstrated how OpenAI's conversation compaction feature could be used to extract a model's hidden reasoning into plain text. The technique bypassed cross-model replay blocks by utilizing the same model for compaction and having cheaper models repeat the output. OpenAI patched the issue on October 23. The company's intelligent systems think step by step internally before responding, but the company keeps that reasoning hidden as encrypted data. In August, measures were taken to prevent these thoughts from being transferred to other systems, but the research team at security firm Xint discovered that another feature, which condenses large conversations, could bypass the restriction. How did the method work?

articles.title: Set up Bedrock model fallback with AgentCore Gateway
articles.excerpt: Setting up a Bedrock model fallback used to be manual work. If you wanted to react to a ThrottlingException or a 503 from Amazon Bedrock, you wrapped InvokeModel in a try/catch, hard-wired a second mo…
articles.body: Setting up a Bedrock model fallback used to be manual work. If you wanted to react to a ThrottlingException or a 503 from Amazon Bedrock, you wrapped InvokeModel in a try/catch, hard-wired a second model and rebuilt that logic in every service. Since October 22, 2026, AgentCore Gateway can take over this job centrally: it now speaks the Bedrock InvokeModel API and, based on a rule, reroutes requests to a backup model when the primary model is throttled, unavailable or too slow. This topic is on my mind because LLM calls are moving from experiment to production dependency in many teams right now. A chatbot that simply shows an error message when it hits a 429 during peak load gets noticed.

articles.title: Nuxt SSR Streaming: Faster TTFB and the Response You Can't Change Later
articles.excerpt: Classic server rendering in Nuxt is all or nothing. The server runs every plugin, resolves every awaited useFetch, renders the whole Vue tree to a string, and only then sends a single byte back. If on…
articles.body: Classic server rendering in Nuxt is all or nothing. The server runs every plugin, resolves every awaited useFetch , renders the whole Vue tree to a string, and only then sends a single byte back. If one API call on the page takes 600ms, the browser sits staring at a blank tab for 600ms, unable to even start downloading your CSS. Streaming SSR has been one of the longest-standing open issues in the Nuxt repo, and as of Nuxt 4.5 it finally ships behind a flag. The win is real, but it comes with a contract change that is easy to trip over. Once the first byte is on the wire, the HTTP status and headers are locked in. Let's look at both halves. Turning it on Streaming is experimental and off by default.

articles.title: How Erlang Developers Can Build a Vibrant Digital Space for Erlang
articles.excerpt: How Erlang Developers Can Build a Vibrant Digital Space for Erlang The Erlang community is recognized for its technical resilience, but the same cannot always be said for its digital presence. While t…
articles.body: How Erlang Developers Can Build a Vibrant Digital Space for Erlang The Erlang community is recognized for its technical resilience, but the same cannot always be said for its digital presence. While the Elixir ecosystem has built a formidable content machine, Erlang — the language that started it all — often remains in the shadow, with solid documentation but little continuous production of accessible, up-to-date content. This article proposes a practical roadmap for Erlang developers who want to change this scenario. The idea is simple: turn technical knowledge into digital presence through three complementary fronts — weekly articles, YouTube videos, and active research on how to contribute better. Why care about Erlang’s “digital space”?

articles.excerpt: Technologies developed to remove space junk and fix broken satellites can be repurposed to build fleets of bodyguard spacecraft to protect important assets from attacks.
articles.body: Technologies developed and tested in orbit to remove space junk and fix broken satellites can be speedily repurposed to build fleets of bodyguard spacecraft to protect important satellites from adversary attacks, space clean-up company Astroscale thinks. Astroscale made history with its 2024 up-close in-orbit inspection of a discarded Japanese rocket stage during the pioneering ADRAS-J mission in low Earth orbit (LEO), the region of space below altitudes of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). The firm's ELSA-D mission , which ran from 2021 to 2024, was the first commercial endeavor to demonstrate orbital capture technologies in LEO. Now, this technology can come in handy as Western space assets face increasing threats from Russia.

articles.body: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.  As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize transformers. New, solid-state versions could help relieve some of the supply concerns and make sure the grid can handle the growing pressure. Conventional transformers generally rely on huge amounts of specialized steel alloys and miles of copper wire to do their work of transferring electricity between circuits.

articles.title: Your Android phone may remember AI chats you thought you deleted
articles.excerpt: Keeping your AI conversations offline doesn't necessarily mean they're gone when you delete them.
articles.body: TL;DR Tech researchers have developed a forensic tool that recovers deleted conversations from AI apps running locally on Android devices. In one experiment, the tool recovered 26 previously shared facts, compared with just 14 accessible to the original AI session. The technique requires forensic access to device data and doesn’t establish that conversations from cloud-based chatbots are similarly recoverable. Recovering deleted information from phones is hardly a new trick. We’ve seen it with text messages , photos, and other supposedly erased data. But researchers have taken things somewhere more intriguing: they’ve developed a forensic tool that can retrieve deleted AI conversations and actually bring the chatbot back to life, complete with some of its previous knowledge.

articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. The Cassini spacecraft would later drop off a probe on Titan named Huygens, which was a European spacecraft that hitched a ride to the Saturn system with the Cassini mission. But before Cassini dropped off its robotic passenger, it flew by Titan a few times and took some amazing photos . Cassini completed its first flyby on July 3, 2004, but when it swung by a second time on Oct. 26, it got about 300 times closer than it did the first time. At the closest point of this flyby, Cassini was 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) away from the surface of Titan. The spacecraft took hundreds of photos during this flyby , and these were the highest resolution views of Titan anyone had ever seen.

articles.title: NASA ends Swift space telescope mission after failed rescue attempt
articles.excerpt: NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift Observatory, after a private satellite failed to meet up with the aging spacecraft in orbit.
articles.body: NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift space telescope, after a private satellite failed in its bold bid to rescue the aging spacecraft. That rescue mission was led by the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies, whose LINK spacecraft tried to meet up with Swift this summer to boost its orbit. That didn't work out, however, so Swift continues its fall back toward Earth. The telescope is expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere "in the next few weeks," NASA said in a statement on Friday (Oct. 23). That statement served primarily to announce the end of the Swift mission after more than 20 very productive years. The telescope launched to Earth orbit in November 2004, tasked with studying gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) — the most powerful explosions in the cosmos.

articles.title: 'Donnie Darko' at 25: How a giant rabbit, time loops, and teen angst became a sci-fi cult classic
articles.excerpt: "28 days, 6 hours, 42 minutes, 12 seconds. That is when the world will end."
articles.body: "Have you ever seen a portal?" The term "cult classic" has been loosely bandied about in cinematic circles until its definition has diluted into nothingness, but never has it been more appropriately applied than to director Richard Kelly’s strange psychological sci-fi thriller, "Donnie Darko", which celebrates its milestone 25th birthday today. Starring Jake Gyllenhaal, Drew Barrymore, Mary McDonnell, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Patrick Swayze, Jena Malone, and Noah Wyle, "Donnie Darko" was released on Oct. 26, 2001, into an unstable world still shocked by the catastrophic Sept. 11 terrorist attacks less than two months earlier.
